target_customer: Aspiring and junior web developers who pay for online coding courses and career paths
problem: Video coding tutorials show code as static pixels so learners cannot interact with it. Scrimba records browser events so learners can pause a screencast and edit the code in place.
business_model: Consumer subscription for courses and paid career paths, plus bootcamp and hiring offerings

founders.name: Per Harald Borgen
founders.background_notes: Quit his job in November 2016 to co-found Scrimba AS after Sindre showed him the prototype (Scrimba blog). Employer not named in opened sources.

founders.name: Sindre Aarsaether
founders.background_notes: Creator of the Imba programming language (2011) and of the first Scrimba prototype (Scrimba blog).

founders.name: Frode Jensen
previous_startups: Adtech company with clients including Conde Nast
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 15 years in online business as CTO, full-stack developer and ops lead, product manager on projects for EA Games and the Boston Marathon.

technical_complexity.rationale: An event-based recording format that replays DOM and editor events in the browser plus a live editor was original engineering, built from the author's own language work.

defensibility.rationale: The scrim format is proprietary and a content library accumulates, but learning content is hard to lock in and free tutorials compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it; the blog says experts called online code learning a race to the bottom. It partnered with Mozilla MDN later.

market_need_then: Strong online demand for coding education. The Scrimba blog reports a free CSS Grid course launched 2017-12-23 took users from about 5,000 to over 15,000 in a week, and a 2019 paid course with Kevin Powell earned about 40 thousand dollars in its first month.

branding.name_origin: A blend of scribble or screencasts with Imba, the programming language its CTO created; the founders' own blog leaves the exact pairing open.

identity.logo: SVG logo marks in black and white variants
identity.mascot_or_character: Pumpkin the cat, team mascot and live stream star; the Imba project has its own pink and yellow mascot

branding.brand_signature: The interactive scrim format and the team cat mascot
branding.community_and_virality: Discord presence confirmed on the team page; reviewers on DEV Community and Medium praise the interactive format. No merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely mentioned in learn-to-code roundups and reviews with a distinctive format, and a viral free course in 2017, but not a mass consumer brand.

pivots.from: Classroom tools, API documentation and developer team communication
pivots.why: Growth was slow until a free CSS Grid course launched 2017-12-23 (Scrimba blog).

outcome_analysis: Scrimba found its market after a 2017 pivot to courses, became profitable in summer 2019 through a paid course, and raised about 540 thousand dollars in October 2020 around YC. It stayed small and capital efficient; in October 2023 Schibsted Ventures bought a 4.5 percent stake from existing owners. It is a durable niche education business without a venture scale raise.
notes: Total raised about 940K per Nordic9 (2020-10); aggregators range 379K to 1.01M. Seedtable lists a 150K 2020-08 round; not confirmed so not recorded. The 2023-10-09 Schibsted Ventures deal is a secondary purchase of 4.5 percent from existing owners with no amount or valuation, so it is not a round. Nordic9 names Magnus Holm as a founder, the YC page names Frode Jensen; both could be early team and are unresolved, only the YC-listed set is recorded. Competitors: current comparison articles (freeCodeCamp, Codecademy, Frontend Masters, Udemy) are 2024 to 2026 and Scrimba's own blog names none, so none are recorded.
